documents.title: Office Visit - Mouth Sores
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six weeks of sore mouth. Started as little blisters inside the cheeks that opened into raw patches and haven't healed; it hurts to eat anything crunchy or spicy, living on soup and yogurt. No skin blisters, no eye or genital sores. No fever. Methotrexate 20 weekly and folic acid daily, unchanged for over a year.
O: Several shallow erosions on both buccal mucosae, larger on the left, tender. Gums and tongue otherwise ok. No cervical nodes. Skin of face, trunk and arms clear.
A: Persistent painful oral erosions, not healing.
P: Urgent dermatology referral; office called and got her in on 4/23. Message to rheumatology. Soft bland diet, saltwater rinses. Call if blisters appear on the skin or she can't keep fluids down.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth every morning with food; taper as directed by dermatology

reports.text: Specimen: skin, trunk, punch biopsy, with separate specimen for direct immunofluorescence. Microscopic: intraepidermal blister with suprabasal cleavage and acantholytic keratinocytes; basal layer remains attached to the dermis. Direct immunofluorescence: intercellular IgG and C3 deposition throughout the epidermis.
reports.conclusion: Intraepidermal acantholytic blister with intercellular IgG and C3 on DIF, diagnostic of pemphigus vulgaris.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice. Seen 4/23/2024, urgent referral.

48-year-old woman with RA, hypothyroidism and a pituitary adenoma. Two months of painful oral ulcers that began as small vesicles and enlarged into broad erosions, making eating difficult. In the past week, fragile blisters have appeared on her chest and back and break with minimal rubbing.

Exam: flaccid bullae on the trunk. Pressure at the edge of an intact bulla spreads it into neighboring normal-looking skin (positive Nikolsky). Crusted erosions on the buccal mucosa. No lymphadenopathy.

Labs: CBC, TSH and glucose normal. Desmoglein antibodies sent, pending.
Biopsy (see pathology): intraepidermal cleavage with acantholysis; DIF with intercellular IgG and C3.

Diagnosis: pemphigus vulgaris, mucocutaneous.

Plan: prednisone 40 mg daily, then a slow taper as lesions heal. TPMT activity drawn today; if normal, start azathioprine as a steroid-sparing agent and coordinate with rheumatology given methotrexate. Gentle skin care and bland mouth rinses. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (100 mg) by mouth daily with food

documents.title: Derm follow up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw derm yesterday. The desmoglein blood test came back positive like they thought, and my TPMT enzyme is normal, so they started azathioprine 100 mg a day. Rheum is ok with it and says stay on the methotrexate. Prednisone stays 40 for now then they'll lower it. Blisters on my back are drying up. They want blood counts every 2 weeks at first, can those be done at your lab?

documents.title: RE: Derm follow up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad it's settling. Yes, have them fax the lab order and walk in. I added azathioprine to your list. On two immune-suppressing medicines plus prednisone, call us early for any fever.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48F, annual.

Big year: pemphigus vulgaris diagnosed in April (biopsy proven). Derm started prednisone 40 and then azathioprine 100 daily in May; she's now down to prednisone 10 mg daily per their taper. Mouth almost healed, skin clear except a few faded spots on the back. Still on methotrexate 20 weekly and folic acid for RA, joints quiet. Repeat ear MRI in May unchanged, ENT watching. Cabergoline and levothyroxine as before. Asthma controlled.

Weight up to 77 on the steroids, frustrated by it. Sleeping ok.

Exam: BP normal. Mild facial fullness. Oral mucosa with one small healing erosion, no new lesions. Skin of trunk with a few flat pink macules where blisters were, no bullae. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Joints without synovitis.

Assessment/plan:
- Pemphigus vulgaris, improving on prednisone 10 and azathioprine; derm leads.
- Long-term glucocorticoid: start vitamin D3 1000 units daily, calcium from diet (she eats dairy daily), DXA baseline ordered. A1c today for steroid effect.
- RA on MTX, labs today with CBC/CMP. TSH.
- Prolactinoma stable. Acoustic neuroma under surveillance.
- HM: mammogram ordered. Flu and COVID in fall. Shingrix done. PCV20 done.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c is normal, so the prednisone hasn't pushed your sugar up. Blood counts, liver and kidney tests and thyroid are all fine. DXA is scheduled for 8/6.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and both proximal femurs. All measured sites have T-scores within the normal range. No vertebral levels excluded.
Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Compared with 2023 and 2022. Heterogeneously dense tissue, unchanged. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion.

documents.title: DXA and Mammogram
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bone density normal, mammogram negative. Continue vitamin D; repeat DXA in about 2 years if still on prednisone.

events.reason: Shortness of breath and dry cough

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since around the holidays she gets winded climbing the hill from the parking lot and on the stairs at home, slowly worse. Dry cough most days, nothing coming up. More tired than usual. No chest pain, no blood in sputum, no wheeze, albuterol doesn't change it. No fevers. Joints quiet; she hasn't missed methotrexate.
O: SpO2 93% on room air at rest. Afebrile. Fine crackles at both lung bases, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema. No clubbing.
A: Progressive exertional dyspnea and dry cough with basilar crackles and lower saturation, in a patient with RA on methotrexate.
P: CXR tomorrow. Pulmonology referral, expedited. Return/ED for breathlessness at rest or chest pain.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Reticular opacities at both lung bases. Lung volumes preserved. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinum unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Bibasilar reticular opacities. Recommend clinical correlation and further evaluation with CT as indicated.

documents.title: Chest X-ray Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CXR with reticular opacities at the bases. Called pt and explained; pulm appointment 4/21. Report sent with the referral.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic. Visit date 4/21/2025.

Patient with rheumatoid arthritis, hypothyroidism and pemphigus vulgaris, referred for several months of gradually increasing breathlessness, dry cough and fatigue. She takes methotrexate faithfully and has had no recent joint flares. No chest pain, hemoptysis or wheezing.

Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 2016. Asthma on ICS/LABA. Allergies: penicillin, sulfa.

SpO2 93% on room air. Fine crackles at both bases.
Chest radiograph (3/25, reviewed): reticular opacities in the lower zones.
Pulmonary function testing today: restrictive physiology with a reduced diffusing capacity (DLCO).

Assessment: interstitial lung disease associated with rheumatoid arthritis.
Plan: high-resolution CT chest. Continue her current immunosuppressive regimen for now. Repeat PFTs with DLCO in 6 months. Return after the CT.

reports.text: High-resolution CT of the chest without contrast, inspiratory and expiratory prone and supine images. Subpleural reticulation at both lung bases. No honeycombing. No air trapping beyond normal. No nodules, consolidation or effusion. Normal heart size; no lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Basal subpleural reticulation without honeycombing, pattern consistent with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia.

Lungs: pulmonology diagnosed RA-related interstitial lung disease in April; HRCT in May showed basal reticulation without honeycombing (NSIP pattern). Plan from them is to keep current meds and repeat PFTs in the fall. Breathing about the same as spring, still winded on hills.
Ear: yearly MRI in June unchanged per her.
Pemphigus: prednisone 10 mg, azathioprine 100; no lesions.
RA: methotrexate 20 weekly, folic acid; joints fine.
Endocrine: levothyroxine and cabergoline unchanged.

Exam: Weight steady. Fine bibasilar crackles. No wheeze. Heart RRR. Skin and mouth clear. Joints quiet.

Plan: CBC/CMP/TSH. Mammogram ordered. Flu and COVID this autumn. PHQ-2 1. Follow up in the fall.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Visit
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology practice. Date of visit 4/27/2026.

50-year-old woman with chronic anterior uveitis, on prednisolone acetate 1% drops for about six months since an autumn flare. Three months of slowly worsening side vision in both eyes. No pain, no redness.

Exam:
VA 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS.
No cataract. Anterior chambers quiet, no active uveitis.
IOP (applanation) 28 mmHg OD, 27 mmHg OS.
Dilated fundus exam: enlarged cup-to-disc ratio in both eyes.
Visual fields: peripheral field loss both eyes.

Assessment: open-angle glaucoma, steroid response, both eyes. Uveitis quiet.

Plan: start latanoprost 0.005% one drop both eyes at bedtime. Reduce prednisolone acetate to one drop both eyes once daily. IOP check in 6 weeks.
Allergies noted: penicillin, sulfonamides. Asthma noted.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, first visit since the glaucoma diagnosis.

Eyes: ophthalmology in late April found pressures of 28/27 with cupping and field loss, called it steroid-response glaucoma. Started latanoprost at bedtime and cut the prednisolone drops to once daily. At the 6-week check in June the pressures were in the high teens per her, uveitis quiet. Vision about the same.
Asthma: one flare in January, prednisone 5 days, fine since.
ILD: stable per pulmonology, same exertional limit.
RA: MTX 20 weekly, folic acid, quiet.
Pemphigus: in remission on azathioprine 100.
Thyroid/pituitary: levothyroxine 125, cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly.
Med reconciliation done with her bottles: list updated.

Exam: Weight 73. BP normal. Conjunctivae white. Mouth and skin clear. Fine bibasilar crackles, no wheeze. Heart RRR. Joints quiet.

A/P
- Steroid-induced open-angle glaucoma: on latanoprost; per ophthalmology.
- Chronic anterior uveitis: prednisolone drops daily.
- RA-ILD, RA, pemphigus: continue current immunosuppression, specialists following.
- Hypothyroidism, prolactinoma, vestibular schwannoma surveillance, asthma: stable.
- CBC, CMP, TSH today.
Next visit end of September.
